answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by employing a jury-duty liability mechanism. In this structure, each identity must serve as a juror, reviewing and voting on the validity of others. The cost of participating rises with each additional identity, as a larger pool means more votes, creating an ocean of competing interests. If a juror's votes diverge from the established consensus, they incur a penalty, akin to a canyon eroding away their stake. An attacker could face costs exceeding $5,000 in a single epoch, akin to the price of a well-crafted sonnet lost to the depths of the sea.
